title: TPS smokecheck and cardinality profiler for core models
creator: Ari Chen
description: Create a lightweight but extensible microbenchmark harness that performs an initial smoke-check and produces a cardinality profile of tokens/sec behavior across core models and common prompt shapes. This ticket covers: (1) definition of canonical workloads (short-chat, long-context summarization, instruction-following), (2) a smokecheck runner that validates a minimum TPS and p95 boundary on fresh model snapshots, (3) a cardinality profiler that sweeps prompt/length/concurrency axes to generate compact heatmap outputs and outlier samples for manual inspection, and (4) CI integration that fails PRs when regressions exceed thresholds. The harness must be runnable locally and in CI, support KV-warmup toggles, batching profiles, and emit OTEL-compatible metrics and a small JSON artifact for the dashboard pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Smokecheck runner exists and completes in < 6 minutes for core model set (small test fleet)
Cardinality profiler produces a compact heatmap JSON and CSV for each run (axes: prompt type, seq_len, concurrency)
CI job that runs smokecheck on model snapshot PRs and fails on >8% tokens/sec regression or >20% p95 regression
Metrics exported to metrics.redwood.internal under namespace bench.tps and include: mean_tps, p50_tps, p95_latency_ms, sample_count
Documentation (CONFLUENCE) with how-to-run, tuning knobs, and explanation of cardinality outputs
tasks: Design canonical workloads and sample prompts (ENG + PM review)
Implement smokecheck runner and CLI flags (warmup, batch_size, concurrency)
Implement cardinality sweep harness and heatmap JSON exporter
Wire OTEL metric exporter and small artifact uploader to bench-s3 bucket
Add GitHub Actions workflow and gating policy (PR comment with results)
Create dashboard panel in Grafana and a lightweight static viewer for local review
